title: Separable Verbs
definition: Some German verbs have a prefix that separates from the main verb in a main clause. The conjugated verb stem stays in its usual position and the prefix moves to the end.

rules.title: Basic structure
rules.explanation: In a simple main clause, conjugate the verb and place its separable prefix at the end.

examples.german: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
examples.english: I get up at seven o'clock.

rules.title: Common separable prefixes
rules.explanation: Common separable prefixes include an-, auf-, ein-, aus-, mit-, ab-, zurück-, and vor-.

rules.title: Conjugation and separation
rules.explanation: The verb stem is conjugated according to the subject, while the prefix remains unchanged at the end.

rules.title: In yes/no and W-questions
rules.explanation: The prefix still goes to the end of a main-clause question.

rules.title: With modal verbs
rules.explanation: When a separable verb is used as the infinitive after a modal verb, it usually stays together at the end.

examples.english: I have to get up early.

common_mistakes.correct: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
common_mistakes.explanation: The prefix moves to the end in a main clause.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ich stehe auf um sieben Uhr.
common_mistakes.correct: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
common_mistakes.explanation: Put the prefix at the end after the other sentence information in this neutral example.
After a modal verb, use the full infinitive.

mastery_goal: You can recognize common separable verbs, separate the prefix in main clauses, and keep the infinitive together after a modal verb.
